FULL TEXT:
Page 1 of 37
Before
UTTARAKHAND ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION
Petition No. 64 of 2026
In the matter of:
Petition for examination of claim of Aggregate Revenue Requirement (ARR) relating to Transfer
Scheme by the Uttarakhand Electricity Regulatory Commission.
In the matter of:
Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd … Petitioner
CORAM
Shri M.L. Prasad Chairman
Shri Anurag Sharma Member (Law)
Shri Prabhat Kishor Dimri Member (Technical)
Date of Order: September 30, 2026
The Order relates to the Petition filed by Uttarakhand Power Corporation Limited
(hereinafter referred to as “UPCL” or “the Petitioner”) for examination of claim of Aggregate
Revenue Requirement (ARR) relating to Transfer Scheme, filed pursuant to the direction issued by
the Government of Uttarakhand (hereinafter referred to as “GoU”) under Section 108 of the
Electricity Act, 2003.
1. Background and submissions
1.1 The Petitioner filed the present Petition under Section 86(1)(a), Section 86(2) and Section 108
of the Electricity Act, 2003, read with Regulation 59 of the UERC (Conduct of Business)
Regulations, 2014.
1.2 The Petitioner submitted that an agenda proposal for filing of additional claim of ARR, as per
Transfer Scheme of Assets and Liabilities executed between Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation
Limited (hereinafter referred to as “UPPCL”) and UPCL and notified by the GoU on
08.03.2022, was put-up by the Petitioner company to the Board of Directors in the 126th Meeting
Page 2 of 37
held on 04.12.2025 wherein the Board recommended that, before filing the Petition, the
Corporation should have its claim examined by the Uttarakhand Electricity Regulatory
Commission (hereinafter referred to as “Commission or UERC”) and for this purpose a
request may be made to GoU to issue directions u/s 108 of the Electricity Act, 2003 to the
Commission, requiring it to examine UPCL’s ARR claim arising from the Transfer Scheme in
accordance with the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003 and the rules and regulations
framed thereunder. The Petitioner submitted that its BoD also directed in the meeting that
once such directions are issued by the GoU to the Commission, UPCL should submit the
requisite details of its claims relating to the Transfer Scheme for examination following which
further action will be taken.
1.3 The Petitioner submitted that on the request of UPCL, Principal Secretary (Energy), GoU vide
its letter no. 419, dated 08.06.2026 at para 11 and 12 has directed the Commission, as follows:
“11. Since the Transfer Scheme has now been formally notified vide Government Order dated 08.03.2022,
the issue requires examination by the Hon’ble Commission in accordance with law. Accordingly,
in exercise of the powers conferred under Section 108 of the Electricity Act, 2003, the Government
of Uttarakhand directs the Hon’ble Commission to examine the additional ARR claim computed by
UPCL in terms of the notified Transfer Scheme of Assets and Liabilities between UPPCL and
UPCL. This direction is issued in the larger public interest, having due regard to the financial
viability of the State distribution licensee and the interest of electricity consumers in Uttarakhand.
12. UPCL shall, upon receipt of this direction, file the complete details of its ARR claim relating to the
Transfer Scheme before the Hon’ble Commission. The Hon’ble Commission may thereupon proceed
to examine the claim and pass such orders as it deems appropriate in accordance with the applicable
law and regulations.”
1.4 The Petitioner submitted that, in compliance of the said direction of the GoU, the Petitioner
company vide its letter no. 3197/UPCL/RM/B-29, dated 10.06.2026 filed the requisite details
of the claim of ARR relating to the Transfer Scheme before the Commission. In turn, the
Commission vide its letter no. UERC/6/TF-854/2026-27/2026/380, dated 17.06.2026 directed
UPCL to file a Petition before the Commission in the matter, in accordance with the provisions
of UERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2014, and accordingly, this Petition is being filed
in compliance of the above provisions of law and in-accordance with the procedure specified
in UERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2014.
Page 3 of 37
1.5 The Petitioner submitted the facts of the case as summarized herein below:
a) The State of Uttaranchal (now Uttarakhand) came into existence on 09.11.2000 in
accordance with the provisions of the Uttar Pradesh Reorganization Act, 2000. Section 63
of the Reorganization Act laid down the broad principles for sharing and transfer of
undertakings, assets, rights and liabilities with respect to the Power sector between the
States of Uttaranchal and Uttar Pradesh. UPCL was established under the Companies Act,
1956 on 12.02.2001 as per the provisions of Section 63(4) of the Reorganization Act.
b) The Government of India (GoI), in accordance with the powers conferred on it under
Section 63 of the Reorganization Act, divided the assets, liabilities, rights and
undertakings of U.P. Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL) and U.P. Jal Vidyut Nigam
Limited (UPJVNL) between them and UPCL and Uttarakhand Jal Vidyut Nigam Limited
(UJVNL) with effect from 09.11.2001 vide its Order No.-42/7/2000-R&R, dated 05.11.2001.
c) On 12.10.2003, a scheme for division of assets and liabilities was executed between UPPCL
and UPCL in accordance with the provisions of GoI Order dated 05.11.2001, showing
Gross Fixed Assets (GFA) of Rs. 1,058.18 Crore.
d) GoU wrote to the Commission on 01.12.2003, stating that the liability of Rs. 572 Crore of
Central Public Sector Undertaking (CPSU) dues and the interest thereof stood shifted from
UPCL to the State Government.
e) The Commission, considering the value of opening GFA of UPCL as Rs. 508 Crore (as
against Rs. 1,058.18 Crore as per the Transfer Scheme), allowed return on equity,
depreciation and interest on loan on the said amount.
f) A liability of Rs. 572 Crore towards power purchase dues on UPPCL (CPSUs) was taken
over by GoU, and GoU, vide Order No.-258/I(2)/2010-05/81/2006, dated 09.02.2010,
accorded the conversion of the said liability into share capital of UPCL. The Petitioner's
consequent claim for return on equity of Rs. 572 Crore was rejected by the Commission
vide Tariff Order dated 24.05.2011 stating as follows:
“Further, the Commission also observed that the issue is related to the finalization of the Transfer
Scheme which can be best examined along with the other aspects such as opening value of Gross Fixed
Assets only upon finalization of the Transfer Scheme.”
Page 4 of 37
g) On the request of the Petitioner, GoU, vide Order No. 117/I(2)/2011-05/19/2002, dated
27.04.2012, approved the Transfer Scheme executed between UPPCL and the Petitioner
on 12.10.2003, considering the value of GFA as Rs. 1,058.18 Crore, however, the
Commission, in the Tariff Order dated 06.05.2013, held that the Transfer Scheme could not
be considered as finalized, as it was only a letter to UPCL from GoU and not a proper
notification on finalization of the Transfer Scheme in accordance with the Uttar Pradesh
Reorganization Act, 2000.
h) In a meeting held on 17.08.2019 between the Chief Secretaries of Uttar Pradesh and
Uttarakhand, the scheme for transfer of assets and liabilities between the two States was
finalized, and UPPCL, vide its letter no. 1677 dated 30.12.2019, made payment of Rs. 1.56
Crore to the Petitioner, the issue having been clarified to be settled forever.
i) On the request of the Petitioner, GoU, vide Order no. 263/I(2)/2022-05-20/2007-TC, dated
08.03.2022, notified the scheme for transfer of assets and liabilities executed between
UPPCL and the Petitioner.
j) In a meeting held with GoU on 05.12.2024, the Petitioner was advised to seek clarification
regarding creation of Regulatory Assets for the claim, to be amortized as per the
provisions of the Tariff Policy of the Ministry of Power (MoP), Government of India, and
to simultaneously file the ARR and Tariff Petition for FY 2025-26, excluding the claim of
Transfer Scheme. The Petitioner requested Power Finance Corporation (PFC) for allowing
creation of Regulatory Assets against the pending claim for the period from 12.10.2003 to
31.03.2023. Further, Secretary Energy, GoU made a similar request to Secretary Power,
GoI. Subsequently, the BoD of UPCL in its meeting dt. 26.12.2024 authorized the
Committee of Directors (CoD) of UPCL for filing the Petition before the Commission in
the matter of transfer of Assets and Liabilities between the UPCL and UPPCL based on
response of M/s PFC/MoP, GoI. However, no clarification was received from MoP till the
date of issuance of the Tariff Order dated 11.04.2025.
k) The Commission, vide its Tariff Order dated 11.04.2025, directed the Petitioner to claim
the impact of the Transfer Scheme along with the next tariff filing, stating as follows:
“The Commission directs UPCL to claim the impact of the transfer scheme, if any, alongwith the next
Page 5 of 37
tariff filing failing which the Commission will not consider any impact of the same.”
l) The Board of Directors of the Petitioner, in its 126th meeting held on 04.12.2025,
recommended that, before filing the Petition, the Corporation should have its claim
examined by the Commission, and that a request be made to GoU to issue directions under
Section 108 of the Electricity Act, 2003 to the Commission, requiring it to examine the
Petitioner's ARR claim arising from the Transfer Scheme.
m) The Principal Secretary (Energy), GoU, vide their letter dated 08.06.2026 directed the
Commission under Section 108 of the Electricity Act, 2003 to examine the additional ARR
claim computed by the Petitioner in terms of the notified Transfer Scheme, stating as
follows:
“Since the Transfer Scheme has now been formally notified vide Government Order dated 08.03.2022,
the issue requires examination by the Hon'ble Commission in accordance with law. Accordingly, in
exercise of the powers conferred under Section 108 of the Electricity Act, 2003, the Government of
Uttarakhand directs the Hon'ble Commission to examine the additional ARR claim computed by
UPCL in terms of the notified Transfer Scheme of Assets and Liabilities between UPPCL and UPCL.
This direction is issued in the larger public interest, having due regard to the financial viability of the
State distribution licensee and the interest of electricity consumers in Uttarakhand.”
GoU, vide the said letter dated 08.06.2026, also directed the Petitioner to file the
complete details of its ARR claim relating to the Transfer Scheme before the Commission
for examination.
n) The Petitioner, vide letter no. 3197/UPCL/RM/B-29, dated 10.06.2026, filed the requisite
details of the claim of ARR relating to Transfer Scheme before the Commission, in
response to which the Commission, vide letter no. UERC/6/TF-854/2026-27/2026/380,
dated 17.06.2026, directed the Petitioner to file a Petition before the Commission in the
matter, in accordance with the provisions of the UERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations,
2014.
o) The Petitioner accordingly filed the present Petition on 20.06.2026.
1.6 The details of claim of Transfer Scheme of assets and liabilities executed between UPPCL and
the Petitioner, as furnished in the Petition, are summarised herein in the Table given below:
Page 6 of 37
Table 1 : Details of claim towards impact of Transfer Scheme claimed by the Petitioner
Particulars Amount (Rs. Crore)
Depreciation 288.70
Return on Equity 521.89
Interest on Loan 115.57
Interest on Working Capital 10.20
Total ARR 936.37
Carrying Cost 4,963.65
Total Claim (including Carrying Cost) 5,900.01
1.7 The Petitioner under the ground of relief stated that the present Petition has been filed as per
the direction issued by GoU vide its letter no. 419, dated 08.06.2026, and sought relief before
the Commission for examination of the same and to pass such orders as it deems appropriate
in the matter.
1.8 Subsequent to filing of the Petition, the Commission, vide letter no. UERC/6/TF-856/2026-
27/2026/629, dated 22.07.2026, directed the Petitioner to submit the methodology/plan of
action for recovery of the proposed claim from the consumers. In response to which, the
Petitioner, vide letter no. 4234/UPCL/RM/B-29, dated 28.07.2026, submitted its reply,
referring to the minutes of the 126th meeting of the Board of Directors held on 04.12.2025, which
records as follows:
“After detailed deliberations, the Board recommended that, before filing the petition, the Corporation
should have its claim examined by the Hon'ble UERC. For this purpose, a request may be made to the
Government of Uttarakhand to issue directions under Section 108 of the Electricity Act, 2003 to the
Hon'ble UERC, requiring it to examine UPCL's ARR claim arising from the Transfer Scheme in
accordance with the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003 and the rules and regulations framed
thereunder. Once such directions are issued by the Government of Uttarakhand to the Hon'ble UERC,
UPCL should submit the requisite details of its claims relating to the Transfer Scheme for examination
following which further action will be taken.”
The Petitioner submitted that, it is clear that as per the decision of Board of Directors,
any further action in the matter shall be taken after the examination of the claim submitted by
the Petitioner to the Commission.
Page 7 of 37
1.9 The Commission also issued Public Notice in the matter to invite comments from the
consumers and stakeholder’s at large and the last date of submission of the comments was
27.07.2026. Subsequently, the Commission also held a Public Hearing in the matter on
02.09.2026 at the Commission’s office.
1.10 The Commission received comments from six stakeholders on the Petition filed by UPCL. The
list of stakeholders who have submitted their objections/ suggestions/comments in writing is
enclosed as Annexure-1.
1.11 Subsequent to the Public Hearing held on 02.09.2026, the Commission, vide letter no.
UERC/6/TF-856/2026-27/2026/908, dated 08.09.2026, communicated to the Petitioner certain
deficiencies/queries observed in the Petition, requiring the Petitioner to submit, inter-alia:
(i) The basis for claiming Return on Equity on the additional claim of GFA of Rs. 550.18 Crore,
having regard to the fact that the liability of Rs. 572 Crore assumed by GoU towards CPSU
dues was not utilised by UPCL in creation of assets.
(ii) Justification for the claim of Carrying Cost of Rs. 4,963.65 Crore and the manner in which
UPCL proposes to recover the same.
(iii) The treatment, in UPCL’s books of account, of the amount of Rs. 1.56 Crore received from
UPPCL vide its letter no. 1677, dated 30.12.2019.
(iv) The reasons for computing the impact of the Transfer Scheme with effect from 12.10.2003,
instead of 08.11.2001, being the date on which the assets stood transferred under the
Transfer Scheme.
(v) The basis and reference documents relied upon by UPCL for the rate of interest considered
for each financial year for computation of Interest on Working Capital and Carrying Cost.
1.12 In response, the Petitioner, vide letter no. 5219/UPCL/RM/B-29, dated 18.09.2026, furnished
its point-wise reply to the above deficiencies. The submissions made by the Petitioner in the
said letter are examined by the Commission at the relevant places in Section 3 (Commission’s
views and decision) of this Order below.
2. Stakeholders’ Objections/Suggestions and UPCL’s Responses
The Commission has received comments/objections on the Petition filed by UPCL for
Page 8 of 37
examination of claim of ARR relating to Transfer Scheme. Since several issues are common and
have been raised by more than one stakeholder, the comments have been clubbed issue-wise
and summarised below.
2.1 General
Stakeholder’s Comments
2.1.1 M/s Galwalia Ispat Udyog Private Limited (GIUPL), M/s Kashi Vishwanath Textile Mill
Private Limited (KVTMPL) and M/s Kumaun Garhwal Chamber of Commerce & Industry
(KGCCI) submitted that passing the impact of the Transfer Scheme in tariff will adversely
impact industrial growth, and that the Commission had already directed UPCL to file the
issue along with the next tariff filing.
Further, Sh. Rajpal Rana submitted that the claim relating to the Transfer Scheme
requires a prudence check before being admitted. He additionally submitted that the Order
of the Commission should maintain a balance between the interests of consumers and the
utility, and should contain reasons/justification for allowances and disallowances.
UPCL’s Reply
2.1.2 In reply, UPCL submitted that the Transfer Scheme was notified by GoU vide Gazette
Notification dated 08.03.2022, and that the present Petition has been filed pursuant to the
direction issued by GoU vide letter No. 419 dated 08.06.2026 in the larger public interest,
through which the State Government, in exercise of its powers under Section 108 of the
Electricity Act, 2003, directed the Commission to examine the financial implications/claim
arising from the Transfer Scheme. Accordingly, the claims have been computed in line with
the applicable UERC Tariff Regulations and Tariff Orders. UPCL further submitted that the
issues raised in the Petition may be considered and decided by the Commission in accordance
with the provisions of the Act and the Regulations.
2.2 Maintainability of the Petition
2.2.1 M/s GIUPL, M/s KVTMPL and M/s KGCCI further submitted that the Petition is not
maintainable, lacks a valid cause of action, invokes wrong and inapplicable legal provisions,
and fails to satisfy statutory requirements, since under Section 108 the State Commission is
Page 9 of 37
only guided by policy directions of the State Government and is not bound to follow
administrative or arbitrary communications. They further stated that Section 86(2) of the
Electricity Act, 2003 is inapplicable as the present matter does not call for the Commission's
advice to the State Government, and also, there is no occasion to invoke Regulation 59 of the
UERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2014.
UPCL’s Reply
2.2.2 In response, UPCL submitted that it has filed the present Petition pursuant to the directions
of the State Government given on 08.06.2026, and that under clause (2) of Section 86
(Functions of State Commission), the State Commission can advise the State Government on
matters concerning generation, transmission, distribution and trading of electricity, or any
other matter referred to it by that Government. Further, the ARR claim has been computed
and presented in accordance with the applicable UERC Tariff Regulations and Tariff Orders
issued by the Commission from time to time, and the Petition has been filed to place the
complete details of the claim before the Commission for examination in compliance with the
directions of GoU.
2.3 Valuation of Gross Fixed Assets and treatment of Equity/CPSU Liability
Stakeholder’s Comments
2.3.1 M/s Industries Association of Uttarakhand (IAU) submitted that the Transfer Scheme
records the underlying asset allocation as based on normative/proportionate formulae rather
than physical verification, and that an independent prudence audit/vintage physical
verification is required before any part of the claim is admitted.
2.3.2 M/s GIUPL, M/s KVTMPL and M/s KGCCI sought clarification as to the value of the assets
actually transferred, and whether UPCL is justified in considering Rs. 1,058.18 Crore as GFA
as per the Transfer Scheme as on 08.11.2001, submitting that assets ought to be booked at
historical cost in accordance with prevailing accounting standards.
2.3.3 M/s GIUPL, M/s KVTMPL and M/s KGCCI further submitted that the value of Rs. 1,058.18
Crore, being based on a normative/proportionate formula under the Transfer Scheme, is a
normative value that cannot be used for computing depreciation, which is required under
the Regulations to be provided only on the historical cost of assets.
Page 10 of 37
2.3.4 M/s GIUPL, M/s KVTMPL and M/s KGCCI additionally submitted that the amount of Rs.
572 Crore cannot be treated as equity of the Government of Uttarakhand in UPCL so as to
attract Return on Equity, since under the Regulations only that equity which is invested in
the creation of fixed assets is entitled to return.
They further submitted that a transfer scheme for sharing of assets and liabilities could
only be given effect to by an order of the Central Government under Section 63(4) of the U.P.
Reorganization Act, 2000, and that the Transfer Scheme dated 12.10.2003, and the GoU letter
dated 27.04.2012 approving it, do not satisfy this requirement.
UPCL’s Reply
2.3.5 In reply, UPCL submitted that it was incorporated on 12.02.2001, and that under the Transfer
Scheme executed on 12.10.2003, GFA of Rs. 1,058.18 Crore was transferred to it. The
Commission, while determining tariff vide Order dated 25.04.2005, considered the opening
GFA of Rs. 508 Crore based on the value claimed by UPPCL in 2001 and accepted on a
provisional basis, and any assessment relating to the opening asset base should be examined
in light of the assets transferred under the Transfer Scheme. UPCL reiterated this position in
response to the queries on historical versus normative valuation for depreciation purposes.
2.3.6 Further, on the query regarding treatment of Rs. 572 Crore as equity, UPCL submitted that a
liability of Rs. 572 Crore was transferred to it against power purchase dues on UPPCL
towards Central Power Sector Undertakings (CPSUs). This liability was taken over by GoU,
which, vide Order No.-258/I(2)/2010-05/81/2006, dated 09.02.2010, accorded conversion of
the said liability into share capital of UPCL. UPCL furnished the following break-up of
funding of the fixed assets transferred as on 09.11.2001:
Table 2 : Break-up of funding of the fixed assets transferred as on

UPCL submitted that, on this basis, it is entitled to recovery of return on equity of Rs.
165.05 Crore (being 30% of Rs. 550.18 Crore not so far considered by the Commission) and
interest on normative loan of Rs. 178.67 Crore (being 70% of Rs. 550.18 Crore less accumulated
depreciation of Rs. 206.46 Crore).
2.3.7 On the query regarding the validity of the Transfer Scheme under Section 63(4) of the U.P.
Reorganization Act, 2000, UPCL submitted that, in exercise of powers under the said Section,
the Ministry of Power, GoI, issued the Order dated 05.11.2001 providing for constitution and
operationalisation of the successor State power utilities, pursuant to which UPCL's
operations were deemed to have commenced w.e.f. 09.11.2001. UPCL reproduced the
relevant provisions of the said Order as follows:
“(4) Nothing in the preceding provisions of this section shall be construed as preventing the
Government of the State of Uttar Pradesh or, as the case may be, the Government of the State of
Uttaranchal from constituting, at any time on or after the appointed day, a State Power Corporation,
an Electricity Regulatory Commission or a State Warehousing Corporation for the State under the
provisions of this Act relating to such Power Corporation, Commission or Warehousing Corporation;
and if such a Power Corporation, Commission or Warehousing Corporation is so constituted in either
of the States before the dissolution of the Power Corporation, Commission or Warehousing
Corporation referred to in sub-section (1)—
(a) provision may be made by order of the Central Government enabling the new Power Corporation,
new Commission or the new Warehousing Corporation to take over from the existing Power
Corporation, Commission or Warehousing Corporation all or any of its undertakings, assets, rights
and liabilities in that State, and
(b) upon the dissolution of the existing Power Corporation, Commission or Warehousing
Corporation—
Page 12 of 37
(i) any assets, rights and liabilities which would otherwise have passed to that State by or under
the provisions of sub-section (3) shall pass to the new Board, new Commission or the new
Warehousing Corporation instead of to that State;
(ii) any employee who would otherwise have been transferred to or reemployed by that State under
sub-section (3), read with clause (i) of sub-section (5), shall be transferred to or re-employed by
the new Power Corporation, new Commission or the new Warehousing Corporation instead of to
or by that State.”
2.4 Carrying Cost, Delay Attribution and Recovery Methodology
Stakeholder’s Comments
2.4.1 M/s IAU and Sh. Rajpal Rana submitted that the delay in implementation of the Transfer
Scheme arose from administrative and institutional actions and is attributable to controllable
factors, namely, the Petitioner's own delay in pursuing formal notification and the delay on
the part of the State Government in issuing the notification. They submitted that the carrying

2.5 FPPCA and its Distinction from the Transfer Scheme Claim
Stakeholder’s Comments
2.5.1 Sh. Rajpal Rana sought clarification as to what is FPPCA (Fuel and Power Purchase Cost
Adjustment), and how the charges recovered under FPPCA differ from the charges claimed
under the Transfer Scheme.
UPCL’s Reply
2.5.2 In reply, UPCL submitted that FPPCA is a regulatory mechanism enabling a distribution
licensee to recover or pass on variations in uncontrollable costs such as fuel, power purchase
and transmission charges incurred during a particular period, whereas, the present claim
under the Transfer Scheme is distinct and relates to ARR components associated with the
fixed assets transferred from UPPCL to UPCL, including Return on Equity, Interest on Loan,
Depreciation and Interest on Working Capital. The Transfer Scheme claim and the FPPCA
mechanism, accordingly, operates in different regulatory domains and addresses separate
cost elements.

3. Commission’s views and decision
3.1 At the outset the Commission clarifies the scope of the present proceedings. The Petition has
been filed by UPCL for examination of the claim of Aggregate Revenue Requirement (ARR)
relating to the Transfer Scheme, and the relief sought by the Petitioner, as recorded in the
Petition, is confined to examination of the said claim by the Commission and passing of such
orders as the Commission deems appropriate in the matter. Accordingly, the present
proceedings, and this Order, are limited to examination of the claim so put forth by UPCL,
and the findings recorded in this Order are for the purposes of such examination alone. This
Order does not entail final determination of tariff for any year, and does not pass any order,
or direction, whatsoever for recovery of any part of the claim examined herein from
consumers. The findings of the Commission recorded hereinafter, including as to the
admissibility or otherwise, in principle, of the components of the claim, shall be given effect
to, quantified, and translated into tariff and recovery, if any, only through the appropriate
mechanism in UPCL's ensuing tariff proceedings, in accordance with the Electricity Act, 2003
and the applicable Tariff Regulations.
